paper_reference.method_note: Implements the paper's upper false-positive loss and lower farsighted loss. Joint candidates are evaluated with simultaneous Hoeffding UCBs rather than the paper's decoupled two-step threshold selection.

notes: All trajectories are synthetic deterministic fixtures; the 512 rows are not independent real observations and no real-world guarantee is claimed.
A trajectory is one calibration unit. Steps within a trajectory are not independent samples.
The finite candidate policy grid is frozen in this fixture before the outcomes are inspected.

For each candidate and each of the two risks, a one-sided Hoeffding UCB uses delta/(2*M) where M is the number of candidate policies. A union bound makes all 2*M bounds simultaneous under iid/exchangeable trajectory-level calibration units.
Upper loss is 1 when an upper-threshold exit emits an incorrect current answer, else 0.
Lower loss at lower-threshold exit t is the fraction of current and future outputs f_t..f_T that would be correct, matching the paper's farsighted false-negative loss.
The selected candidate minimizes mean normalized compute among candidates whose two simultaneous risk UCBs meet the two declared budgets. No monotonicity assumption or binary search is used.
Distribution shift, adaptive candidate generation after observing calibration labels, task-group conditional guarantees, and sequential online recalibration are out of scope.
